Use GTAPViz with AI Assistants (MCP)

Pattawee Puangchit

2026-11-20

Source: vignettes/GTAPViz_AI.Rmd
GTAPViz_AI.Rmd

GTAPViz includes an MCP server (Model Context Protocol), so an AI assistant such as Claude, Cursor, VS Code Copilot or Gemini CLI can use GTAPViz on your computer. You describe what you want in plain language; the AI loads your .sl4/.har results, makes the figures and tables, and saves the R code it ran as a script you can rerun at any time.

“Load my results in D:/project/in, plot welfare (EV) and real GDP by region, and make a welfare decomposition chart. Put Thailand first.”

What you need

  • R (free, https://cran.r-project.org) and GTAPViz. You do not need to know R: the AI writes and runs the code.
  • An AI app that supports MCP, for example Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code or Gemini CLI.

One-time setup

Open R (or RStudio) and run:

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("Bodysbobb/GTAPViz")   # the AI feature needs GTAPViz 1.3.0 or later
GTAPViz::mcp_install()                         # Claude Desktop

The AI feature is currently available from GitHub. No extra tools (such as Rtools) are needed; the other packages are installed from CRAN automatically.

Then fully quit Claude Desktop (including from the system tray or menu bar) and open it again. GTAPViz now appears in the app’s tools menu.

For other apps:

GTAPViz::mcp_install("claude_code")   # Claude Code (all projects)
GTAPViz::mcp_install("cursor")        # Cursor
GTAPViz::mcp_install("other")         # prints settings to paste into any MCP app

After updating R: run GTAPViz::mcp_install() again, because the settings point to the R installation that ran it.

Try it

Start with the bundled example data:

“Use GTAPViz to load the example data and show me the welfare (EV) results by region.”

Then use your own results by giving the folder that holds your .sl4 and .har files:

“Load the GTAP results in D:/TradeWar/in. Which experiments are there?”

“Plot qgdp, EV and tot by region, with the regions on the vertical axis.”

“Show the welfare decomposition as stacked bars and rename alloc_A1 to ‘Allocative efficiency’.”

“Make an Excel table of all regional results with experiments as columns.”

“Which sectors in SEAsia have the largest output changes? Plot the top 10.”

The AI checks the variables and values before plotting, looks at a preview of each figure, and adjusts the style when labels overlap. Figures (PNG, and PDF on request) and Excel tables are saved in an out folder next to your input folder.

Experiments, the -WEL file suffix and an OutputMapping.xlsx workbook in a map folder are detected automatically, following the project layout described in the Data vignette.

Reproducible R script

Every action is run as ordinary GTAPViz code and added to gtapviz_session.R in the output folder. Running that script in R recreates every figure and table without the AI, so the results can be checked, shared and cited. Ask “show me the R script” to see it in the chat. An excerpt:

library(GTAPViz)

# ---- Step 1: Load GTAP results (EXP1, EXP2) ----
input_path <- "D:/TradeWar/in"
output_path <- "D:/TradeWar/out"
auto_gtap_data(
  experiment = c("EXP1", "EXP2"),
  input_path = input_path,
  har_suffix = "-WEL",
  mapping_info = "GTAPv7",
  plot_data = TRUE
)

# ---- Step 2: comparison_plot of sl4.plot.data[["REG"]] (EV, qgdp) ----
comparison_plot(
  data = sl4.plot.data[["REG"]],
  filter_var = list(Variable = c("EV", "qgdp")),
  x_axis_from = "Region",
  output_path = output_path,
  export_picture = TRUE,
  plot_style_config = create_plot_style(color_tone = "purdue")
)

Privacy

  • The MCP server runs on your computer and only talks to the AI app that started it. No account, key or server of the package author is involved.
  • Your .sl4/.har files are read locally. What a tool returns (summaries, numbers you ask about, figure previews) becomes part of your conversation with the AI provider you chose, like anything you type there.
  • By default the AI can only use GTAPViz functions. mcp_install(allow_r_code = TRUE) additionally lets it run any R code, for custom data work.

What the AI can do

Task Tools
Find and load results find_gtap_files, load_gtap_results, load_gtap_dynamic (recursive dynamic)
Inspect data describe_data, view_data
Figures comparison_plot, detail_plot, stack_plot, map_heatmap, trend_plot, decomp_area_plot
Tables report_table (Excel), pivot_table (Excel pivot table)
Prepare data rename_values, sort_data, convert_units
Style and script style_options, get_r_script, gtapviz_help

Troubleshooting

  • GTAPViz does not show up in the app: quit the app completely and reopen it. In Claude Desktop, check Settings > Developer for the server status and log.
  • “There is no package called GTAPViz”: install GTAPViz in the R version used by mcp_install(), then run mcp_install() again.
  • Other MCP apps: GTAPViz::mcp_config() prints the command and settings to paste.
